collection.title: Promotion-gated contemporary consciousness supplement candidates
collection.promotion_rule: Every proposed new row has at least two distinct authoritative or primary works, a reviewed identity boundary, and a kind from the catalog allowlist. Two locators do not imply evidential independence or truth.
collection.identity_policy: COGITATE is excluded as a standalone record and represented only as claim-level evidence additions for the existing GNWT and IIT records. De-duplicate those additions against existing profile-enrichment packets before registration.
collection.registration_policy: This file is a review artifact only and must not be added to catalog.json automatically.

records.name: Curing Coma Disorders-of-Consciousness Common Data Elements
records.status_note: A harmonization framework for variables and metadata, not a diagnostic scale or theory.
records.summary: The Curing Coma Campaign CDE framework standardizes research variables across behavioral phenotyping, hospital course, neuroimaging, electrophysiology, biospecimens, physiology, interventions, outcomes, family goals, and pediatric work.
records.scope: Interoperable data collection for coma and disorders-of-consciousness studies.
records.boundary_note: Do not catalog as a measure of awareness. Its function is dataset comparability and reporting consistency.

claim_scope.target: Standardized representation of DoC research variables.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A patient's state, prognosis, or a mechanism of consciousness.

basis: International working-group process, official versioned materials, and peer-reviewed overview.
limitations: Adoption, completion burden, interoperability, and psychometric validity vary by element.
evidence_profile.independence: The two sources document the same program from scholarly and official perspectives; they establish identity and versioning, not independent outcome validation.

open_questions: Which elements most improve cross-cohort reproducibility?
How will version changes and missingness be represented?

records.name: Simplified Evaluation of CONsciousness Disorders
records.status: validated in initial and multicenter cross-cultural cohorts
records.status_note: An eight-item bedside instrument; not a replacement for repeated comprehensive and multimodal assessment.
records.summary: SECONDs is an eight-item standardized bedside assessment designed to identify diagnostic signs of consciousness more rapidly than the CRS-R. The defining 57-patient study was followed by a 60-patient, three-center Italian validation with repeated blinded assessments.
records.scope: Rapid behavioral assessment of patients with disorders of consciousness.
records.boundary_note: Retain as a named abbreviated scale adjacent to, not merged with, CRS-R. A negative behavioral result cannot exclude covert consciousness.

claim_scope.target: Observable behaviors used in clinical DoC classification.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: Absence of covert consciousness when command-following behavior is absent.

basis: Multicenter Italian cross-cultural validation in 60 patients with repeated blinded assessments.
limitations: Speed trades away some sampling depth; results remain dependent on arousal, motor output, examiner training, and repeated testing.
evidence_profile.independence: The Italian study used different lead investigators but included collaborators from the original expert network; it is a distinct cohort, not fully independent intellectual replication.

open_questions: How does serial SECONDs perform across etiologies and acute settings?
What multimodal escalation rule should follow an indeterminate screen?

records.name: Lucidity and Consciousness in Dreams Scale
records.status_note: Retrospective phenomenology scale; it is not physiological verification of lucid dreaming.
records.summary: LuCiD measures eight dimensions of dream experience: insight, control, thought, realism, memory, dissociation, negative emotion, and positive emotion.
records.scope: Multidimensional retrospective characterization of ordinary and lucid dreams.
records.boundary_note: Do not merge LuCiD self-report with signal-verified lucid-dream paradigms or infer lucidity from one high subscale alone.

claim_scope.does_not_establish: Online physiological state, report accuracy, or a mechanism of dream consciousness.

limitations: Recall, selection, and demand effects; objective state verification is external to the scale.
evidence_profile.independence: The later Spanish study used a different author team and sample, providing genuine independent psychometric evidence for that adaptation.

open_questions: How stable are factors across cultures and induction methods?
How do LuCiD dimensions map to preregistered physiological markers?

records.name: Targeted Dream Incubation protocol
records.status_note: A cueing-and-awakening protocol for N1 hypnagogia, not general dream control or lucid dreaming.
records.summary: TDI uses state-sensitive auditory cues during sleep onset, followed by repeated awakenings and dream reports, to increase incorporation of a target theme into hypnagogic experience. A follow-up experiment related theme incubation to post-sleep creative performance.
records.scope: Closed-loop incubation and sampling of targeted content during N1 sleep onset.
records.boundary_note: Distinguish this protocol from broad dream engineering and from ocular-signal verified lucid dreaming.

claim_scope.target: Probability that a cued theme appears in immediate hypnagogic reports.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: Precise control of dream narratives, lucidity, or direct readout of experience.

basis: Controlled follow-up relating targeted incubation to creative performance.
limitations: Small selected samples, subjective reports, suggestion effects, and imperfect N1 detection.
evidence_profile.independence: The two distinct studies share the same core laboratory and proponents; external replication remains needed.

open_questions: How specific is cue incorporation under blinded scoring?
What safety and consent standards apply to repeated closed-loop use?

records.name: AI Consciousness Test
records.status_note: A language-based proposal designed for training-restricted systems; not a validated diagnostic.
records.summary: ACT proposes increasingly demanding natural-language questions about internally experienced and consciousness-related concepts, ideally administered to an AI whose training has been restricted to reduce learned imitation of human discourse about consciousness.
records.scope: Behavioral evidence for consciousness in language-capable artificial systems under controlled training conditions.
records.boundary_note: The authors characterize passing as sufficient but not necessary evidence; that sufficiency claim is philosophical and contested, not experimentally established.

claim_scope.target: Spontaneous grasp of consciousness-related concepts under restricted exposure.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A substrate-independent gold standard, applicability to nonlinguistic systems, or immunity to hidden training contamination.

basis: Later monograph chapter elaborating the test and its rationale.
limitations: Language dependence, false negatives, gaming, auditability of training, and the gap between discourse and experience.
evidence_profile.independence: The two works share Susan Schneider and elaborate the same proposal; no empirical gold-standard validation exists.

open_questions: Can restricted training be verified in modern foundation models?
What response criteria avoid anthropocentric grading?

profiles.status_note: COGITATE is an evidence/profile update, not a new framework record. Its preregistered comparison supported and challenged selected GNWT predictions; it did not decide the whole theory.

basis: A preregistered, multisite fMRI/MEG/iEEG adversarial collaboration tested selected GNWT and IIT predictions in 256 participants.
limitations: The experiment tests agreed operationalizations and auxiliary assumptions; it does not globally validate or refute GNWT.
evidence_profile_additions.independence: Theory proponents participated in prediction design while a theory-neutral consortium executed the study; this reduces but does not eliminate interpretive dependence.

profiles.status_note: COGITATE is an evidence/profile update, not a new framework record. It tested selected IIT-linked predictions but not the full IIT 4.0 causal formalism.

basis: A preregistered, multisite fMRI/MEG/iEEG adversarial collaboration tested selected IIT and GNWT predictions in 256 participants.
limitations: The study did not compute a full IIT 4.0 Φ-structure and cannot decide the theory's constitutive identity claim.
evidence_profile_additions.independence: Theory proponents participated in prediction design while a theory-neutral consortium executed the study; auxiliary-assumption and interpretation disputes remain.
